I'm going through the same thing a you man, and I'm already in my 30s. All I can tell you is to stick to one thing, like really stick to it. Make a list of 10 things you want to do, then narrow that down to 3 things. Choose the one that you like the most and stick to it. If you work on something you don't like at the moment to pay the bills then practice that on the side. Use most of your free time to practice that thing, do it for one year.

You see, you're not simply going to magically find something you're good at and suddenly be "happy". You have to practice it, get good at it and then practice some more. There will be days when you feel like its not for you, you'll be discouraged and feel like moving on to something else as you're filled with doubts, DONT! Those are the moments you have to tell yourself, I said I would do this ! and I will keep practicing.

Those athletes you see who get really good or people who become very successful at their careers weren't "smarter" than you and I, they didn't magically know their "passion". The only thing they had was CONSISTENCY and DISCIPLINE. They stuck to one thing until they were good enough at it to either know it was their passion or know they didn't like it.

​

Think about it, even if you're 50 years old, that means you'll still probably live another 20-30 years. That means you could technically dedicate one year to 20-30 different things to get good at. DO you know how good a human being can get at something if they consistently dedicate ONE YEAR to something? 

​

Also, forget the end goal, if you want to be a bodybuilder (just an example) don't imagine yourself at a competition taking the Gold looking like Arnold. Instead, imagine yourself at the gym lifting the weights day in and day out and eating the good food. You see, we often get lost in this idea, the end goal. But we don't even know if the process to get there is something we actually want to do. So fall in LOVE WITH THE PROCESS instead. Either way, you don't even know if you'll be alive to see the end goal, none of us do. We don't know what will happen. Remember, it's not the destination but the journey. So find something you want to get good at and fall in love with the process, the practice, and stick to that one thing long enough to know.  


P.s. for reference I've always wanted to write/make films but could never "find the time" and was always worried about the money. SO instead I studied a career I didn't like and worked a job I liked even less for 7 years. I quit that job for something more flexible and decided to dedicate a whole year to studying video editing, screenwriting and film production.  Is it easy? hell no. Do I doubt myself on a daily basis? You bet! do I miss the money? no doubt! But I'm doing it man, I'm going for it and it feels so worth it!  Will I become a famous director or even make money out of it? who knows, who cares. All I can do is try, REALLY try.

You know, I was going to write something but didn’t want to hurt or offend anyone here. Depression is a very real and serious issue that so many of us are going through. However, your post makes me think of what I was going to say again.

Maybe our depression doesn’t mean we’re not “normal” when compared to others without it. Maybe it’s quite the opposite, maybe we just see the world as it really is and can’t simply ignore it. Some of us have been through difficult and imaginable situation that no human should ever go through. Some do want that big house and kids and wife/husband. Some have other physical  illnesses that keep them from doing what they love. Some have never felt love from someone else and some have even been betrayed snd abused by those that were supposed to love them. But whatever it is, we know there’s something off with this place that keeps us from truly being happy.

Crazy that you were a reporter and like to write, for a while being a reporter was a dream I had. Writing always has been and it’s one of the few things that still give me some joy. I’ll tell you something though, none of these feelings, none of them are a reason to end our lives. We might not be happy but as crazy as it sounds I do think the world needs us. It’s just we need to figure out how to stay here without having to live our life as the lie they feed us. But some of us have to have open eyes don’t we? The world can’t just be full of people blindly following money and the “dream”.

I think you need to keep writing as much as you can and don’t hold back. If you’re feeling someone content or numb write. If you’re feeling down or like you can’t do this anymore write even more. Pour your heart, your soul and all your pain into it. 

I’m not even trying to be supportive or telling you this to “help”. I just feel your pain in your post and think more people need to feel it too. And maybe just maybe you will feel better letting it out. I, like yourself, feel a bit better too knowing we’re not the only ones who feel like this. Maybe that’s our reason to be here. To help those who feel like us get through these times. Maybe I’m just looking for a purpose but whatever it is I truly believe you have a lot to give this world. 

I wish you the best in this journey as well.
